newsitem.title: UK: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.
newsitem.headline: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week May 23 - May 30, 1997.
FRANKFURT - Flaghafen said it is seeking to set up and lead a German airport alliance.
LONDON - BA said it is planning to sell nearly half of its 14.65 pct stake in Galileo International, the global computer reservation system.
MINNEAPOLIS - Great Lakes Aviation, operating as United Express said it will resume a limited service to five cities in Iowa and Illinois, ending a voluntary suspension of service that began May 16.
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa's Public Enterprise and Transport Ministry said it had received four non-bidding bids for the privatization of Sun Air
MOSCOW - A cancellation of a customs ban on transit cargo through Moscow's airports increased market activity, but air cargo rates were stable, forwarders said.
PRAGUE - The Czech Republic and Vietnam signed two agreements to limit double taxation and to allow better access for each county's air transport, Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said.
MADRID - Spanish development minister Raefael Arias Salgado said a plan to expand Barcelona airport by building a third runway would be ready by the summer.
AMSTERDAM - The Dutch airfreight forwarders association said Dutch airfreight shipments are expected to rise by 12 pct in 1997.
ZURICH - Panalpina said it assumed the current year would be another successful year based on results for the Q1 of 1997.
PARIS - Marseille airport authority said air cargo flown in April down 18.7 pct.
SEOUL - Korean Air Lines (KAL)was the dominant air cargo importer and ex Korea cargo carrier during Q4 1996, said the Korea International Freight Forwarders Association.
*KAL - Is studying new destinations to Miami and Houston to strengthen its American cargo market said vice president and general manager Ji Young Lee.
NICE - Nice-Cote d'Azur airport said it planned to appoint a freight marketing officer later this year.
LUXEMBOURG - Cargolux said freight from Europe, Africa and the Middle East rose 12.6 pct in 1996
LONDON - AirRep said a 20 tonnes cargo capacity, Antonov AN-12 would be based at Manston's Kent International Airport from May 30.
CARACAS - Viasa carrier may fly again under a proposed $50 million joint venture with Pan Am said former Viasa pilots.
HOUSTON - Continental Airlines offered its pilots' union a 38 pct wage increase in a new labour contract said an airline spokesman.
HONG KONG - Cathay said it had suspended operations of its 11 Airbus Industrie A330-300 aircraft due to concerns about the reliability of their Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engines.
*Cathay said it is cancelling six flights out of Hong Kong and expects to cancel a further 10 returning flights due the suspension of its 11 A330-300.
*Cathay said air cargo moving ex-UK will be unaffected by the decision to suspend its A330-300 flights in Asia.
HONG KONG - Dragonair said it had suspended operations of its four A330-300 due to concerns about engine reliability .
*Dragonair said it has cancelled seven flights and rescheduled eight due to the suspension of its A330-300 aircraft.
JAKARTA - Garuda intends to continue flying its six A330-300 aircraft despite concerns by other carriers about their Trent 700 engines.
SINGAPORE - Singapore and Brunei signed an air service agreement in Singapore the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore said.
DENVER - Maverick Airways said it would suspend scheduled services this week for an undetermined period, pending a restructuring
HONG KONG - Cathay said it cancelled 18 flights after grounding 11 of its A330-300 aircraft.
*Cathay said it expected most of its grounded A330-300 aircraft to be back up and running within three weeks.
SYDNEY - Qantas said it would restructure its senior management with effect from June 1, part of an ongoing cost cutting programme.
MOSCOW - Yuzhno Sakhalinsk airport said it would be closed for 36 hours for runway repairs said an aviation official.
NICOSIA - Cyprus Airways is looking at a seven million pound loss in 1997 and possible bankruptcy by 1999 said Takis Kyriakides chairman.
HONG KONG - The Hong Kong civil aviation said it urged Garuda to suspend its Airbus A330-300 fleet because of engine problems.
MILAN - Air One denied it was in talks with BA whereby the British group would take over the Italian company.
VIENNA - Austrian Airlines has won cartel authority clearance to buy a 35.9 pct voting stake in former rival Lauda air, chief executive Mario Rehulka said.
BUCHAREST - Tarom airline denied reports in the local press saying the company had given up plans to renew its fleet.
COPENHAGEN - SAS said it planned to start direct flights between Copenhagen and Newark, New Jersey from May 30.
DUBAI - Emirates airline said it would start daily flights to Manchester on June 1 and to Jo'burg on July 1.
FRANKFURT - SAS said it will start code-share flights with Lufthansa between Cologne and Copenhagen on June 2.
STOCKHOLM - Iceland's Keflavik airport ,air cargo rose 18.5 pct in April compared to the same month 1996.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa Cargo said it will introduce a time-sensitive, money back performance guarantee for Flash express shipments from Germany to all destinations world wide from June 1.
FRANKFURT - Danzas said it has renamed its German subsidiary Danzas Warehousing & Distribution as Danzas Logistic.
NEW YORK - Laguardia Airport saw a 92 pct decline in air cargo imports and exports in 1996 said the airport authority.
JERUSALEM - FedEx said it would begin flying cargo to and from Israel on its own planes next week.
LONDON - The FTA transport activity survey for April 1997 said British air cargo imports and exports is expected to increase in the next quarter
PARIS - Aero Cargo International said it had been appointed GSA for Ceskoslovenske Aerolinie (C.S.A.), effective June 1.
FRANKFURT - Korean Air Lines said its German cargo division has taken over responsibility for freight sales in Scandinavia.
NEW YORK - Air New Zealand cargo sales manager John Reidy it has seen a 50 pct growth at New York's JFK Airport in air cargo traffic since June 1996.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa Airplus said the lack of an air cargo industry electronic reservations system was holding back development of its electronic cargo payment card.
*Lufthansa said it has launched a purchase card for corporate buying of services or goods.
*Lufthansa Airplus improved net profits 18 pct to 16.6 million marks last year.
AMSTERDAM - KLM said it is aiming to expand into eastern Africa following the open skies agreement between the Netherlands and Kenya.
MIAMI - FedEx said it had reached agreement with Arrow Air and Florida West International Airlines to purchase their all-cargo frequency allocations to Argentina.
PARIS - Air France Cargo said it had developed a software tool which would speed up customs clearance operations for freight arriving at U.S. gateways.
PARIS - The French unit of Lufthansa Cargo said net revenues from exports totalled 160 million francs in 1996, an increase of 13 pct on 1995.
NEW DELHI - Air India said it is to start a new route to Chicago via Heathrow from May 30 and restore two flights to Toronto.
WASHINGTON - Airbus Industrie said it will not consider exclusive purchase agreements with airlines, altering comments made by a company spokeswoman last week.
CARACAS - American Airlines said it will add an extra daily round-trip Miami/Caracas flight on June 15 due to rising Venezuelan demand.
CARACAS - Continental Airlines will resume direct flights to Venezuela Oct. 1, after an absence of 15 years, with service between Houston and Caracas, company officials said.
HONG KONG - Rolls-Royce said no other aircraft types have experienced the engine problems of the Airbus A330 planes.
BOSTON - Logan International Airport said it handled 11.4 pct more cargo in Q1 1997 compared with Q1 1996.
VILNIUS - Lithuanian Airlines (LAL) expects to sign an agreement in July to sell 11 YAK 42 aircraft to Pakistan's Bhoja after experts evaluate the planes in June, a LAL official said
FRANKFURT - Total air cargo handled at Duesseldorf airport (DUS) rose 85.7pct in April the airport authority said.
FRANKFURT - Cologne air cargo grows 24.2 pct in April 1997 the airport authority said.
LUXEMBOURG - Cargolux said overall cargo load factor in 1996 totalled 90.2 pct compared to 89.4 pct in 1995.
ZURICH - Swissair said it would offer eight new destinations in the U.S. from June 1.
LONDON, British World Airlines said in a statement it has ordered a pair of new AIR(BAe)ATPs to its fleet.
FRANKFURT - Total flown air cargo handled at Hamburg airport in April rose 1.4 pct the ADV German airports association said.
SOFIA - Bulgaria's Transport Minister Wilhelm Kraus said funding has been found for selecting a consultant for the sale of Balkan Airlines.
KARACHI - Pakistan International Airline (PIA) said it had good prospects for growth in the Far East.
COPENHAGEN - SAS said that its traffic on the key Copenhagen-Stockholm route was unchanged in May, despite new competition from Maersk Air and Finnair.
KIEV - Ukrainian and Uzbekistan's state-owned carriers signed an agreement to make joint flights to New York, senior Air Ukraine officials said
FRANKFURT - The sale of the remaining German airline Lufthansa will begin in the autumn, the government development agency Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW) said.
FRANKFURT - The German air cargo market grew 8.5 pct in April said the German airports association.

MOSCOW - Air traffic controllers at the west Siberian city of Tyumen began an indefinite strike closing the airport to domestic flights but not affecting long-distance flights in-transit over Tyumen airspace.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa said cargo saw a 0.5 pct decline in its freight load factor to 67.2 pct in April over the same month last
SANTIAGO - LAN Chile has signed a contract to purchase three new Boeing 767 for $300 million and has taken out an option to buy two more in 1999, LAN President Jorge Awad said.
MONTREAL - Operating profit for the world's scheduled airlines dropped to 4.3 pct of revenues in 1996 from 5.1 pct in 1995, the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) said.
TOKYO - ANA said that Kichisaburo Nomura will be its new president, instead of the previously announced president-designate Kenzo Yoshikawa.
HONG KONG - Cathay Pacific said it may seek compensation from Rolls-Royce for losses incurred from the grounding of its fleet of Airbus A330 aircraft because of engine problems.
*Cathay said it was operating 90 pct of its flights despite the grounding of its A330-300 aircraft.
ROSLYN HEIGHTS - Kintetsu World Express said Masahiko Goka has been named senior vice-president operations of the U.S. division of the global freight forwarder.
SAN FRANCISCO - Fritz Companies said in a statement that it has opened full service offices in Karachi and Lahore, under the name Fritz Companies Pakistan.
MANAMA - DAS Air Cargo plans a weekly DC10 freighter service to Bahrain, the Gulf Arab state's Civil Aviation Affairs said.
KUALA LUMPUR - Malaysia Airline said it sold two aircraft in the 1996/97 financial year.
MADRID - Air cargo traffic at the 39 airports managed by AENA (Spanish Airports and Air Navegation), rose 10.5 pct in April AENA said.
*Cargo traffic at Barajas airport rose 14.8 pct in April compared to the same month last year.
PARIS - Air France said it made a small profit last year it first since 1989 and the airlines management renewed a plea for privatisation.
DARIEN, Conn - Air Express said it has established a joint venture in Korea through the acquisition of 50 pct Korea Air Freight Ltd.

JOHANNESBURG - The names of shortlisted parties for the upcoming privatisation of domestic carrier Sun Air will not be announced on Friday as originally scheduled, a Transport Ministry spokesperson said
ROME - Cargo and mail traffic at Fiumicino Leonardo de Vinci and Ciampino airports fell by 4.7 pct the Rome airport authority said.
ROME - Alitalia and Continental Airlines said in a statement a second code-shared will operate from June 2 between Rome-Fiumicino and New York-Newark airports.
ROME - International Tourist Representative(I.T.R. Srl) has been appointed as the cargo general sales agent for Continental Cargo from June 1st I.T.R Srl said in a statement.
PARIS - Full freighter flights at the Paris airports Q1 of 1997 rose 21.8 pct on the same period last year the airport authority said.
ROME - Alitalia said it will restart flights from Rome to Addis Ababa on June 3 following a five year break.
PARIS - KLM is poised to choose Lyon-Satolas airport as the site of its proposed freighter sub-hub in eastern France, industry sources said.
LONDON - DHL country manager for Bosnia-Herzegovina Edin Emso said express carrier firms should be able to fly cargo direct to Sarajevo by the end of June.
REDWOOD CITY - DHL says it has begun operating a new weekly cargo charter flight between Miami and San Pedro Sula, Honduras, for New York-based Antillas Air.

PARIS - A euters survey showed the withdrawal of fuel surcharges mid-April gave Air France scope to increase ex-Paris rates on some key Far East routes earlier this month but overall these look stable untill the autumn.
AMSTERDAM - KLM cargo will launch a new trial express service in July for shipments under 30 kgs, a KlM spokesman said. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
